overall_summary: Bitcoin is holding near 78k through US-Iran strikes and oil spikes, with Saylor hinting at fresh buys for support. Hawkish Fed signals, rising yields, a firmer dollar, and ETF outflows still point to near-term pressure on risk assets. Geopolitical noise and a crypto hack add to the cautious tone ahead of key data.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Snap Nine-Day Inflow Streak With $202M Outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs posted about two hundred two million dollars in net outflows on Friday, ending a nine-day run that had pulled in over three billion. Bitcoin pulled back from recent highs near eighty-one thousand and is holding around seventy-seven to seventy-eight thousand. Traders should watch whether this is just profit-taking after a strong month or the start of softer institutional demand, especially with Fed hike odds rising and the jobs report ahead.
items.impact: Near-term pause in bid; tests support after strong August inflows

items.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $78K as U.S. Strikes Iran, Oil Surges
items.summary: U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil higher and pressuring stocks and gold. Bitcoin barely reacted and held near seventy-eight thousand, staying on track for its strongest month since late twenty twenty-four with gains around twenty-three percent. This resilience versus traditional risk assets matters for traders viewing Bitcoin as a macro hedge amid geopolitical and rate uncertainty.
items.impact: Supports decoupling narrative and monthly strength

items.title: Saylor Posts 'We're Back,' Hints Strategy Resuming BTC Buys
items.summary: Michael Saylor posted 'We're Back' alongside Strategy's Bitcoin holdings tracker, a signal that has often preceded new purchases after a two-month pause. The firm holds over eight hundred forty thousand Bitcoin now sitting roughly two point eight billion in profit at current prices. Traders care because Strategy remains one of the largest and most consistent corporate buyers, and a return to accumulation could add meaningful demand.

items.title: Metaplanet Moves Hundreds of Millions in BTC to Coinbase
items.summary: Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet transferred thousands of Bitcoin worth well over one hundred eighty-eight million dollars, and more in subsequent moves, to Coinbase Prime. CEO confirmed the shifts are for custody, not sales, as the company holds about forty-three thousand Bitcoin. Large on-chain moves like this can spark sell rumors and short-term volatility even when clarified as non-selling.
items.impact: Whale flow watch; limited confirmed selling pressure

items.title: Cronos Halts After $75M Tectonic Oracle Manipulation Hack
items.summary: The Crypto.com-linked Cronos chain halted block production after an attacker manipulated the illiquid TONIC token roughly one hundred times and drained an estimated seventy-five million from the Tectonic lending protocol. Only about six million escaped to Ethereum before the freeze. This is a major DeFi and ecosystem hit that can weigh on broader crypto risk appetite even if Bitcoin itself is less directly exposed.
items.impact: Negative for crypto sentiment and altcoin liquidity

items.title: Luke Dashjr Exits Ocean Mining Pool Over Vision Split
items.summary: Longtime Bitcoin developer Luke Dashjr has left Ocean mining pool by mutual agreement, resigning leadership roles as the parent company bought back his equity. He plans a new venture called Convoy focused on decentralizing mining after differences over Bitcoin mining's future and recent protocol issues. Mining pool shifts matter for hashrate distribution and long-term network health though immediate price impact is limited.

items.title: Warsh Hawkish Jackson Hole Lifts September Hike Odds
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole speech stressed that inflation remains sticky and financial conditions are not restrictive enough, with rates as the main tool. Markets priced September rate-hike odds up near 55 to 60 percent from around 35 percent. Two-year yields jumped over 10 basis points and the dollar strengthened, pressuring risk assets including Bitcoin. Traders should watch for any follow-through or fade in these higher-for-longer expectations ahead of next week's jobs data and the September FOMC.
items.impact: Higher rates and stronger dollar headwinds for crypto and equities

items.title: China August Manufacturing PMI Rises to 49.8
items.summary: Official Chinese manufacturing PMI climbed to 49.8 in August from 49.2, beating forecasts around 49.5 and showing slower contraction. Production and new orders both moved back above 50, with large firms expanding. This offers a modest positive signal for global growth and commodities demand even as the reading stays below the expansion threshold. Crypto traders should note any lift to risk sentiment or China-related assets from the improving momentum.
items.impact: Supports risk appetite and commodity-linked markets

items.title: German August CPI Edges Higher to 2.9 Percent
items.summary: Preliminary German consumer price inflation rose to 2.9 percent year-over-year in August from 2.8 percent in July, with state-level data confirming the uptick. The reading keeps Eurozone inflation sticky and may reinforce ECB caution. Combined with US hawkishness it sustains higher global rate expectations. Watch for any euro weakness or bond market reaction that spills into dollar strength and crypto pressure.
items.impact: Supports tighter policy pricing and stronger dollar bias

items.title: Treasury Yields Hold Elevated After Warsh Spike
items.summary: US 10-year yields hovered near 4.71 to 4.73 percent early Monday after Friday's jump on the Warsh speech, while two-year yields stayed elevated on higher hike odds. The curve showed some bear flattening. Elevated yields raise discount rates and borrowing costs, typically weighing on growth assets. Crypto traders need to monitor whether yields break higher toward 4.75 percent resistance or stabilize into the week’s data.
items.impact: Higher yields pressure valuations across risk assets

items.title: US Dollar Index Firms Near 99.6 on Rate Bets
items.summary: The DXY held around 99.5 to 99.7 after Friday's sharp gains driven by Warsh's hawkish tone and higher September hike probabilities. It remains stronger than pre-speech levels even with slight Monday easing. A firmer dollar often coincides with tighter global financial conditions and softer crypto prices. Traders should track USDJPY near 160 and any intervention risks or further dollar upside if data stays hot.
items.impact: Stronger USD typically negative for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: Markets Eye Dallas Fed and Upcoming ISM, NFP
items.summary: Today's Dallas Fed manufacturing survey is due, following Friday's surprisingly weak Chicago PMI drop to 47.1. ISM manufacturing arrives Tuesday and the August jobs report Friday, with expectations for a rebound in payrolls after July's decline. Soft manufacturing readings could temper rate-hike bets while a solid NFP would reinforce the hawkish Warsh message. Crypto traders should prepare for volatility around these releases as they shape Fed path pricing into September.
items.impact: Data-dependent swings in rate expectations and risk sentiment

items.title: US Strikes Iran Hormuz Launchers; Tehran Hits Jordan Bases
items.summary: US forces hit Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after spotting IRGC prepping sea mines, the first direct military action in a month. Iran retaliated with missiles on US bases in Jordan. Oil jumped over two percent with Brent back above ninety dollars as shipping traffic stayed severely reduced. Traders should care because another flare-up in the six-month war keeps the energy risk premium alive, feeds inflation fears, and pressures risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Oil spike and renewed Hormuz risk premium hit risk assets

items.title: Trump Venezuela Oil Deal Aims to Refill SPR and Cut Prices
items.summary: The Trump administration is advancing a deal giving the US majority effective control of more than sixty-five billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves through a private joint venture covering seventeen fields. Interim Venezuelan leadership welcomed it as bringing roughly one hundred billion dollars in investment. Trump has tied the barrels to restocking the Strategic Petroleum Reserve drawn down in the Iran war and lowering US gasoline prices. For crypto traders this is a potential medium-term supply offset to Middle East disruption if production can actually ramp.
items.impact: Longer-term energy supply relief could ease inflation and support risk assets

items.title: US Escalates Iran Sanctions, Targets UAE Bank Channels
items.summary: Treasury is pressing Operation Economic Outcast, proposing to cut Banque Misr’s UAE branches from the US financial system over alleged Iranian shadow-banking flows and sanctioning related facilitators. Secretary Bessent is pushing G20 counterparts to isolate Tehran further while China remains defiant as the top buyer of Iranian oil. The campaign aims to choke remaining revenue after the naval blockade. Markets watch whether secondary sanctions spread to bigger players and raise global financial friction.
items.impact: Tighter pressure on Iran could shorten conflict or spark China retaliation

items.title: Putin, Xi and Iran’s President Meet at SCO Summit
items.summary: Leaders including Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian, India’s Modi and others gather in Bishkek for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. Bilateral talks are expected on energy, the Ukraine war and the Iran conflict amid heavy sanctions on Moscow and Tehran. The meeting underscores a tightening non-Western bloc. Crypto and risk traders note any signals of deeper energy or financial coordination that could blunt US sanctions leverage.
items.impact: Axis coordination may prolong sanctions resistance without immediate market shock

items.title: Russia Strike Kills 38 Near Kyiv; Energy Attacks Threatened
items.summary: A Russian strike on an ammunition warehouse west of Kyiv killed at least thirty-eight people in the deadliest attack of the year there, with secondary blasts devastating nearby homes and a care facility. Russia signaled preparation for massive strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The war continues to grind with heavy drone and missile use. Persistent European conflict remains a background drag on risk sentiment and energy security.
items.impact: Ongoing war and energy targeting sustain risk-off undertone

items.title: US Generals Warn Prolonged Iran War Drains Readiness
items.summary: A classified assessment and Washington Post reporting show senior military leaders formally warning Defense Secretary Hegseth that extended large-scale Iran operations are unsustainable. Stocks of interceptors and precision munitions are heavily depleted and Navy readiness is strained, weakening deterrence elsewhere including the Pacific. The administration is shifting emphasis toward economic pressure and the blockade. This caps the probability of unlimited escalation and keeps the conflict in a war-of-attrition mode that markets have partially priced.
items.impact: Limits to kinetic campaign may stabilize but not remove the risk premium
